papers.title: A Hidden Markov Model Based Framework for Recognition of Humans from Gait Sequences
papers.authors: Sundaresan, Aravind and RoyChowdhury, Amit and Chellappa, Rama
papers.motivation: Walking sequences vary in timing and observed phase.
papers.idea: Model gait as a sequence of latent temporal states.
papers.techniques: Hidden Markov models; silhouette features; sequence likelihood matching.

provenance.basis: Survey text and the recorded literature evidence

papers.abstract: In this paper we propose a generic framework based on hidden Markov models (HMMs) for recognition of individuals from their gait. The HMM framework is suitable, because the gait of an individual can be visualized as his adopting postures from a set, in a sequence which has an underlying structured probabilistic nature. The postures that the individual adopts can be regarded as the states of the HMM and are typical to that individual and provide a means of discrimination. The framework assumes that, during gait, the individual transitions between N discrete postures or states but it is not dependent on the particular feature vector used to represent the gait information contained in the postures. The framework, thus, provides flexibility in the selection of the feature vector. The statistical nature of the HMM lends robustness to the model. In this paper we use the binarized background-subtracted image as the feature vector and use different distance metrics, such as those based on the L/sub 1/ and L/sub 2/ norms of the vector difference, and the normalized inner product of the vectors, to measure the similarity between feature vectors. The results we obtain are better than the baseline recognition rates reported before.

papers.title: Silhouette analysis-based gait recognition for human identification
papers.authors: Wang, Liang and Tan, Tieniu and Ning, Huazhong and Hu, Weiming
papers.motivation: Remote human identification needs cues that do not require facial detail.
papers.idea: Recognize individuals from the shape and evolution of silhouettes.
papers.techniques: Silhouette analysis; gait feature extraction; identity matching.

provenance.basis: Survey text and the recorded literature evidence

papers.abstract: Human identification at a distance has recently gained growing interest from computer vision researchers. Gait recognition aims essentially to address this problem by identifying people based on the way they walk. In this paper, a simple but efficient gait recognition algorithm using spatial-temporal silhouette analysis is proposed. For each image sequence, a background subtraction algorithm and a simple correspondence procedure are first used to segment and track the moving silhouettes of a walking figure. Then, eigenspace transformation based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to time-varying distance signals derived from a sequence of silhouette images to reduce the dimensionality of the input feature space. Supervised pattern classification techniques are finally performed in the lower-dimensional eigenspace for recognition. This method implicitly captures the structural and transitional characteristics of gait. Extensive experimental results on outdoor image sequences demonstrate that the proposed algorithm has an encouraging recognition performance with relatively low computational cost.

papers.title: Silhouette-based human identification from body shape and gait
papers.authors: Collins, Robert T and Gross, Ralph and Shi, Jianbo
papers.motivation: Body shape and walking motion offer complementary remote identity cues.
papers.idea: Use silhouette observations to combine shape and gait evidence.
papers.techniques: Silhouette templates; body-shape descriptors; gait comparison.

provenance.basis: Survey text and the recorded literature evidence

papers.abstract: This baseline identifies people by comparing silhouette key frames extracted from walking cycles. Normalized correlation and nearest-neighbor matching use body proportions and motion-dependent shape without an elaborate articulated model. Evaluation across four datasets examines varying viewpoints, backgrounds, walking styles and image resolutions, providing a reference point for more complex methods.

papers.title: Recognising Humans by Gait via Parametric Canonical Space
papers.authors: Huang, P.S. and Harris, C.J. and Nixon, M.S.
papers.motivation: Gait observations require a compact discriminative representation for comparison.
papers.idea: Map gait patterns into a parametric canonical space.
papers.techniques: Canonical-space projection; gait parameterization; identity classification.

provenance.basis: Survey text and the recorded literature evidence

papers.abstract: Based on principal component analysis (PCA), eigenspace transformation (EST) was demonstrated to be a potent metric in automatic face recognition and gait analysis by template matching, but without using data analysis to increase classification capability. Gait is a new biometric aimed to recognise subjects by the way they walk. In this article, we propose a new approach which combines canonical space transformation (CST) based on Canonical Analysis (CA), with EST for feature extraction. This method can be used to reduce data dimensionality and to optimise the class separability of different gait classes simultaneously. Each image template is projected from the high-dimensional image space to a low-dimensional canonical space. Using template matching, recognition of human gait becomes much more accurate and robust in this new space. Experimental results on a small database show how subjects can be recognised with 100% accuracy by their gait, using this method. q 1999 Elsevier Science Ltd. All rights reserved.

papers.title: Using gait as a biometric, via phase-weighted magnitude spectra
papers.authors: Cunado, David and Nixon, Mark S and Carter, John N
papers.motivation: Individual leg-motion patterns may support biometric identification.
papers.idea: Represent periodic motion with phase-sensitive spectral descriptors.
papers.techniques: Model-based motion analysis; phase-weighted magnitude spectra.

provenance.basis: Survey text and the recorded literature evidence

papers.abstract: This early model-based approach describes leg movement using an articulated pendulum interpretation. The Hough transform estimates leg orientations, least-squares fitting smooths incomplete measurements, and Fourier analysis characterizes their periodic variation. Phase-sensitive spectral features are classified with nearest-neighbor matching to investigate the identifying information carried by walking dynamics.

papers.title: Analyzing and recognizing walking figures in XYT
papers.authors: Niyogi and Adelson
papers.motivation: Walking contains distinctive motion structure across space and time.
papers.idea: Analyze walking figures through their trajectories in an XYT volume.
papers.techniques: Spatiotemporal patterns; walking-motion analysis; identity comparison.

provenance.basis: Survey text and the recorded literature evidence

papers.abstract: This work analyzes walking through the patterns it creates in space and time. Rather than recovering body structure independently in each frame, it uses characteristic motion signatures to constrain a simple articulated representation. These temporal patterns provide a basis for detecting walkers and investigating differences between individuals' gait.
